sections.title: Sound of er
paragraphs: The letters er make the vowel sound in (fern) /fɜːrn/, which means a green plant. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. These letters have two sounds.

sections.title: How to say er
paragraphs: For the first sound, keep your tongue in the central part of your mouth. A central vowel is a vowel where the tongue is in the middle of the mouth. Curl the tongue tip slightly back and keep your lips neutral. For the second sound, make a short, weak schwa with the tongue relaxed. A schwa is a short, weak vowel in the middle of the mouth.

sections.title: Spelling of er
paragraphs: In stressed syllables, er makes the long sound heard in (fern) /fɜːrn/ and (term) /tɜːrm/. A stressed syllable is a syllable that you say with more strength. In unstressed syllables, er makes the short sound heard in (water) /wɔː.tər/ and (butter) /bʌ.tər/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not trill your tongue when you say er. A trill is a consonant where the tongue taps many times very fast. Do not open your mouth too wide like the vowel in cat. Keep your tongue relaxed in the centre of your mouth.
